title: Extraction of Fungal Hyphae: The Sieving and Sucrose Centrifugation Method
author: Isabelle Elisabeth Metzen
materials: The solutions were shaken by hand to resuspend the particles; alternatively, the samples could be vortexed. Equal volumes of 70% sucrose were then carefully injected beneath the aqueous solution using a syringe fitted with a 7 cm long plastic tube (0.5 cm diameter).
Autoclaved pipette tips with low retention were used.

steps.title: Prepare soil suspension
steps.instruction: Place 25–300 g soil in a beaker, add deionized water to a total volume of 400 mL (4 °C), and mix manually with a spoon to detach hyphae.

steps.title: Initial sieving (8 min)
steps.instruction: Place the suspension on the first sieve of the sieving convoy, pump 4 °C water through the system at 2.5 bar and 75 % of maximum power (≈2.25 mm oscillation amplitude at 50 Hz), and run for 8 minutes.

steps.title: Secondary sieving (6 min)
steps.instruction: Remove the 630 µm, 400 µm, and 315 µm sieves, then continue sieving the remaining material for an additional 6 minutes.

steps.title: Collect 40 µm sieve residue
steps.instruction: Transfer particles retained on the 40 µm sieve into 50 mL microcentrifuge tubes and keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Adjust tube volume
steps.instruction: Add deionized water (4 °C) to each tube as needed to bring the total volume to 20 mL.

steps.title: Centrifuge and recover interphase
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 2000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4 °C; using a syringe with tubing, hold the tubing at the interphase of the supernatant and pellet and suction until both solutions are completely collected.

steps.title: Filter hyphae for length assay
steps.instruction: Pipette 2 mL of the hyphae/spore suspension onto a 1.2 µm nitrocellulose filter placed in a manifold holding system connected to a vacuum pump.

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry filter
steps.instruction: Apply vacuum to remove any remaining liquid from the filter.

steps.title: Ink staining
steps.instruction: Immerse the filter with hyphae and spores in an ink solution for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Rinse, dry, and count
steps.instruction: Aspirate the ink through the vacuum, rinse the filter with deionized water, let the filter dry, then count hyphal intersections with the grid at 13 sites under a Leica DM 1000 LED microscope using 10× magnification.

steps.title: Calculate hyphal length density
steps.instruction: Calculate hyphal length density using the equations from Tennant (1975) and Shen et al. (2016).

steps.title: Wash and standardize sample
steps.instruction: Place the collected material on a 40 µm sieve, gently spray it multiple times with deionized water using a spray bottle, collect the washed material in a 15 mL centrifuge tube, and adjust the final volume to 10 mL for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Lyophilize hyphae
steps.instruction: Transfer 8 mL of the hyphae‑containing water solution to a lyophilizer and freeze‑dry the sample.

steps.title: Extract DNA from lyophilized hyphae
steps.instruction: Extract DNA using the MP Biomedicals SpinKit for soil according to the manufacturer’s protocol, modifying the homogenization step: run the Precellys 24 tissue lyzer twice, each for 30 seconds at 6200 rpm.
